The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an “orange” alert warning of rainfall for parts of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Telangana as Cyclonic Storm Akvan intensified into a severe cyclonic storm over the
Bay of Bengal on Wednesday, with landfall expected along the Andhra Pradesh coast on November 20.
The storm is likely to intensify further into a “very severe cyclonic storm” by the evening of November 19 before crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Visakhapatnam around noon on November 20, according to the IMD's November 18 cyclone bulletin.
The weather department has forecast maximum sustained wind speeds of 120-130 kmph, gusting to 145 kmph, at landfall.
The orange rainfall warnings for November 20 cover five districts each in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha. In Andhra Pradesh, these include Alluri Sitharama Raju, Kakinada, Parvathipuram Manyam, Srikakulam and Vizianagaram. In Odisha, the districts are Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Malkangiri and Koraput. In Telangana, four districts- Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Mahabubabad and Suryapet- are under orange warnings for November 20 and 21. Several other districts have yellow warnings.
The IMD has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places in coastal Andhra Pradesh on November 19 and 20, with isolated extremely heavy rainfall also likely. Odisha is expected to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places between November 19 and 21, while eastern Telangana could see similar conditions on November 20 and 21.

Ahead of the cyclone, the Odisha government has restricted beach tourism and recreational activities along vulnerable coastal areas.
Special Relief Commissioner (SRC) Rajesh P Patil has directed the tourism department to suspend boating, water sports, pleasure cruises and other sea-based tourist activities at vulnerable coastal locations. Authorities have also been asked to restrict public access to unsafe beaches, seafronts, jetties and coastal viewing points.
Hotels, resorts and tour operators have been instructed to alert guests, avoid outdoor excursions, follow evacuation or shelter directions and maintain emergency contacts and essential supplies. The restrictions will remain in force until the IMD withdraws its warnings and district authorities certify that conditions are safe.
The state is also preparing to evacuate more than 200,000 people from vulnerable areas, particularly landslide-prone hilly regions in southern Odisha.
Six districts Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Kandhamal, Malkangiri and Koraput—have been identified as highly vulnerable to landslides. District administrations have estimated that 204,070 people may need to be moved to safer locations, with Ganjam accounting for the highest number at 121,597, officials said.
The state has identified 1,902 vulnerable locations across 87 blocks in eight districts and 3,329 cyclone shelters for possible evacuation. More than 2,500 pregnant women have also been identified, of whom over 100 have already been shifted, officials said.
In Rayagada, the district administration has identified around 55 landslide-prone villages for pre-emptive evacuation. The Harabhangi and Badanalla dam projects have also started releasing water to lower reservoir levels and create capacity to accommodate excess rainfall.
Rough seas, strong winds along Odisha coast
The IMD has forecast wind speeds of 40-50 kmph along and off the Odisha coast from the night of November 18, increasing to 50-60 kmph, gusting to 70 kmph, from November 19 until November 20. Sea conditions are expected to remain rough to very rough during this period.
Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea along and off the Odisha coast, while fishing operations have been suspended in the affected parts of the Bay of Bengal.

Cyclone Akvan track revised towards north Andhra, south Odisha for November 20 landfall (Photo: PTI)
Severe Cyclone Akvan has changed course and is now expected to cross the North Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts and South Odisha coast between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha by noon on November 20, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said on Wednesday. The weather department has issued a Red warning for the coastal regions of North Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and South Odisha.
The revised forecast marks a shift from the IMD's earlier prediction on Wednesday morning, when it had said the cyclone was likely to make landfall between Nellore and Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh around noon on November 20. The weather office subsequently revised the projected landfall corridor northwards, placing it between Narsapur and Puri. It also lowered its estimate of the maximum sustained wind speed from 100-110 kmph, with gusts of up to 120 kmph, to 90-100 kmph, gusting to 110 kmph.
At 2.30 pm on Wednesday, the severe cyclonic storm was centred over the westcentral and adjoining central parts of the South Bay of Bengal. It had moved north-northwestwards at a speed of 8 kmph over the preceding six hours.
The system was approximately 520 km southeast of Narsapur, 560 km east of Chennai, 570 km south-southeast of Kalingapatnam, 660 km south of Gopalpur and 720 km south of Puri, the IMD said.
The cyclone is likely to continue moving north-northwestwards before crossing the North Andhra Pradesh and Yanam and South Odisha coasts by noon on November 20. All schools and Anganwadi centres in Ganjam, Gajapati, Puri, Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara and Kandhamal districts have been closed on November 19-20 in view of Cyclone Akvan.
HEAVY RAINFALL WARNING FOR WEST BENGAL
The cyclone is also expected to influence weather conditions in West Bengal, with the IMD forecasting thunderstorms and heavy rainfall in several districts between November 19 and 21.
Purba Medinipur and Paschim Medinipur are likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall, while heavy rain is forecast in South 24 Parganas, Howrah, Jhargram and Bankura districts.
Kolkata is also likely to witness thunderstorms from November 19 to 21, with wind speeds ranging between 30 and 40 kmph during the period.
The meteorological department has advised fisherfolk not to venture into the sea along and off the West Bengal coast on November 19 and 20, as sea conditions are expected to remain rough.
The IMD has warned of the approaching cyclone along the North Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and South Odisha coasts, with the system expected to cross the coast as a severe cyclonic storm by noon on November 20.

Orange alert for AP as Akvan nears coast
In Short
Cyclone Akvan threatens AP with 145-kmph winds, 21-cm rainfall
Amaravati: Andhra Pradesh is bracing for a potentially devastating cyclone as Cyclone Akvan, currently over the south-central and west-central Bay of Bengal, is gathering strength and moving towards the state's coastline. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an Orange Alert for Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha, warning of a very severe cyclonic storm capable of producing wind speeds of 120-130 kmph, gusting up to 145 kmph.
After remaining stationary for nearly nine hours, the system resumed movement and was travelling at just 3 kmph on Tuesday.
Located approximately 650 km from Machilipatnam and 660 km from Visakhapatnam, it is expected to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by Tuesday evening or night and a very severe cyclonic storm by Thursday morning. It is likely to cross the coast between Nellore and Tuni on Friday afternoon (November 20), although the precise landfall location remains uncertain. The threat is particularly serious as several coastal districts are still recovering from the successive impact of Cyclones Arnav and Murasu barely 20 days ago. With groundwater levels already high, even moderate additional rainfall could trigger severe flooding. The IMD has forecast extremely heavy rainfall exceeding 21 cm in isolated places in Konaseema, East and West Godavari, Eluru, Krishna and Bapatla districts, besides Yanam. Heavy to very heavy rainfall is expected across several other coastal districts on November 19 and 20, with rainfall activity continuing in some areas until November 21.
Coastal winds are expected to reach 60-70 kmph from Wednesday evening before intensifying to 120-130 kmph, with gusts up to 145 kmph during landfall. Storm surges of 1-2 metres above normal tidal levels could inundate low-lying areas in Prakasam, Bapatla, Krishna, West Godavari, Konaseema and Kakinada. INCOIS has identified Machilipatnam, Repalle, Avanigadda and Razole as particularly vulnerable. Sea waves could exceed 14 metres.
Danger Warning Signal No. 2 has been issued at several ports. Fishermen have been prohibited from venturing into the sea until November 20. Authorities are preparing evacuations, SDRF and NDRF deployment and relocation of pregnant women to hospitals. Residents in vulnerable areas have been advised to move to rehabilitation centres, secure weak structures and stock drinking water, medicines, flashlights and power banks. The cyclone threatens crops, particularly paddy, banana, papaya and coconut etc, salt pans, electricity and telecommunications infrastructure. Rail, road and air services may also be regulated. Disaster management, RTGS, irrigation, electricity and health departments are on alert. Officials are monitoring the system through Doppler radars at Machilipatnam, Chennai and Visakhapatnam and urging people to remain indoors and follow official advisories.
